A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DEO research work. All main-text and supplementary material, including equations, tables and figures, supports comparison; relocated references and appendix content were matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original DEO experiments on segmentation, change detection and classification, together with component ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: V3 retains those experiments and adds original alignment measurements, controlled variants, robustness testing and resource measurements in Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: The proposed Swin-based DEO retains its multispectral EMA teacher, frozen optical teacher, separate input embeddings, projection heads and training objectives. The new MIM, no-coding-rate and ViT experiments evaluate alternatives rather than revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: The fMoW pretraining sources and all 13 downstream datasets remain unchanged. Appendix D.3 adds an artificially shifted pretraining scenario, extending coverage to input misalignment without introducing another dataset or downstream task.

E2.justification: The external baseline roster in Tables 1–7 and teacher choices in Table 6 are unchanged. New Table 15 adds controlled comparisons against DEO using MIM, omitting coding-rate regularization and using a ViT-S backbone.

E3.justification: Appendices D–E substantially extend the evaluation design with quantitative kernel alignment, controlled objective and regularizer comparisons, artificial input shifts, a parameter-matched Swin-T versus ViT-S comparison, and resource measurements. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged. Some new procedures, especially alignment sampling and shift magnitude, are unspecified.

E4.justification: V3 adds direct tests of contrastive versus MIM training, the necessity of coding-rate regularization, robustness to misalignment and dependence on backbone architecture, alongside quantitative latent-space alignment and compute analyses. These substantially expand the original component, teacher-choice and low-data studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experiments. V3's additional results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–7 and qualitative results are unchanged, but substantial supplementary findings are added. Appendix D.1 reports optical alignment of 0.65 for DEO versus 0.49 for Copernicus-FM. Table 15 reports overall scores of 69.72 for contrastive DEO, 67.28 with MIM and 68.25 without coding-rate regularization, plus backbone and shift results. Table 16 adds resource and emissions estimates.

T1.justification: The objectives and coding-rate/Cholesky mathematics in Equations 1–7 remain substantively unchanged. Replacing union notation with plus notation still denotes concatenating views. The added empirical analyses introduce no new formal results or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same dual-teacher contribution, objective-compatibility claim and optical/multispectral performance claims. The stated average improvements remain 3.64, 1.2 and 1.31 percentage points.

C2.justification: V3 interprets lower multispectral alignment as integration of additional spectral information, attributes avoidance of collapse without coding-rate loss to the optical teacher, and explains locality restoration through patch-token distillation. It also interprets the new robustness and efficiency findings. The original teacher-strength, spatial-alignment and SAR limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 replaces 'Code: TBA' with a project-page link, describes the teachers' training-data provenance in Appendix A.3, and identifies carbontracker for emissions estimation. Existing hyperparameter, dataset-split and learning-rate information is retained. The PDF alone does not establish what resources the project page provides.

R1.justification: V3 adds Liu, Qu and Zhang's 'Multispectral scene classification via cross-modal knowledge distillation' to the related-work citations. Appendix A.3 expands discussion of existing teachers and their training sources; the central positioning against MIM-based EO pretraining remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized language edits, standardizes terminology and notation, and adds supplementary cross-references. It places the supplementary material before the references and expands its section structure, while retaining the main paper's organization and most prose.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 15–16, regroups and renumbers existing appendix tables, and consolidates Figures 5–8 onto one page. Existing figures and their qualitative examples are retained, with limited caption edits and page-layout changes rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens support for the central objective-compatibility argument through the controlled MIM comparison and quantitative alignment analysis, supplementing v1's PCA visualization and component ablations. The regularization and backbone controls also improve the evidence. However, incomplete alignment, shift and resource-measurement protocols limit the new conclusions, and uncertainty reporting remains absent. The net improvement is useful but limited.
